12. Applying It

This repository ships data and stylesheets, never a framework's theme code: a theme belongs to the product that runs it, next to the framework version it was written for (the decision). Every path below is from the root of a release; keep the release's folders side by side when you vendor them, because css/base.css finds the braces in brace/ and css/fonts.css finds the fonts in fonts/.

A Page in Plain HTML and CSS

Take tokens/tokens.css, css/fonts.css with fonts/, and css/base.css with brace/, and load them in that order:

<link rel="stylesheet" href="brand/css/fonts.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="brand/tokens/tokens.css">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="brand/css/base.css">

The page then runs under Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self': the fonts and the brace masks come from its own origin, and nothing needs an inline style. The specimens are built exactly this way. Set data-theme="light" or "dark" on the root to pin a theme, and --nc-brand with data-brand="tenant" for a tenant's color.

A Documentation Site on Starlight

Take tokens/tokens.css, css/fonts.css with fonts/, and css/starlight.css, and name them in Starlight's customCss, in that order. css/starlight.css sets Starlight's own custom properties (--sl-*) from the tokens: the colors of both themes, the two families, the type sizes, the headings of a long-form page, the shadows and the layout's widths. Starlight's inverted text on the accent, its primary link button and its search field's focus border are pairings the contrast gate measures for any tenant's color. It holds no rule for Starlight's markup. The rules that make the sidebar's current page a latched key, a code block a screen and a callout an alert depend on the markup of one Starlight version, so they live in the documentation toolchain, beside the version they were written for. Set the reading voice there too. Starlight sets no size on running text, which keeps the browser's 16 pixels. Its --sl-content-width, 50 rem in css/starlight.css, bounds the content panel, listings and tables included, not the measure of running text. In the toolchain's own rules, set running text in the reading role, 17 pixels, on the 41 rem --nc-measure, as .prose does in css/base.css.

Take syntax/instrument-screen.json for the code blocks. It is Expressive Code's syntax theme, which colors code as a screen does: keywords lit, literals amber and comments dimmed. Each color is the custom property of its role, so tokens/tokens.css decides it, a tenant's color included. One theme serves both page themes, because a screen is the same in both. Name it in the toolchain's ec.config.mjs:

import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { defineEcConfig } from '@astrojs/starlight/expressive-code';

const screen = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL('./src/brand/syntax/instrument-screen.json', import.meta.url), 'utf8'));

export default defineEcConfig({
  themes: [screen],
  useStarlightDarkModeSwitch: false,
  useStarlightUiThemeColors: false,
  minSyntaxHighlightingColorContrast: 0,
});

Keep minSyntaxHighlightingColorContrast at 0: Expressive Code's correction can't compute with a custom property, and the contrast gate holds each role at 4.5 to 1 on the screen. The frame around a code block, Expressive Code's styleOverrides, stays in the toolchain with its other rules (the decision).

A Material UI Application

Take mui/instrument.json, tokens/tokens.mjs with tokens.d.mts, tokens/derive.mjs with derive.d.mts and derive.vectors.json, and css/fonts.css with fonts/. The theme, its createTheme call and its component overrides, stays in the application, under its own type check and tests.

  • mui/instrument.json holds the palette of each scheme for NCode's own brand, with every color role under instrument; the typography variants, each set in the type role that names its use, while one it does not name, such as caption, keeps Material UI's size; the radius, the space scale and Material UI's spacing unit of 8; the 25 elevations as no shadow and four of Instrument's depths: flush, raised, floating and overlay; the durations, the easings and the breakpoints.
  • The palette's secondary takes the colors a tenant's secondary color drives, chosen for how Material UI paints them: main as text on the page and its sheets, in a text or outlined key, a checkbox, a switch and a tab's indicator, and contrastText on main and on dark, a contained key at rest and touched. In the light theme main is the screen, contrastText is on-screen and dark is screen-raised. In the dark theme the screen is about as dark as the page, so main is screen-lit, contrastText is the screen and dark is on-screen-secondary. The contrast gate measures each of these pairings in its theme for every brand, and tokens/derive.mjs holds them for any color.
  • For a tenant, call deriveBrand(primaryColor, secondaryColor) from tokens/derive.mjs and take its light and dark colors for the primary, screen and scope roles. It never throws: a primary it cannot read falls back to NCode Blue and a secondary to the primary, and adjusted names any color it moved to reach its contrast floor.
  • Assert tokens/derive.vectors.json in the application's tests, so a vendored copy is proven to derive what this release derives.
  • Import css/fonts.css once in the application's entry: a bundler emits the four font files beside it, and a page served under font-src 'self' loads them. Vendor each family's license, fonts/OFL-Instrument-Sans.txt and fonts/OFL-Martian-Mono.txt, with its font files: the SIL Open Font License asks every copy of a font to carry it.

An Email

Take email/instrument.html: an HTML email in the light theme with every value written inline, its key and its screen in NCode's colors or a tenant's. It has no <style> element, no custom property and no web font, because most email clients drop all three: its type falls back from Instrument Sans and Martian Mono to the reader's system faces. It lays out one column, 600 pixels wide, in tables, which Outlook on Windows needs. It asks the client for the light scheme alone, and a client that forces a dark scheme still inverts it (the decision).

Fill each slot, a name in double braces such as {{ heading }}, with your template engine, and escape each value as HTML. Mustache, Handlebars, Liquid, Scriban and Fluid read the slots as variables: Mustache and Handlebars escape a value, and the others need their escape filter.

SlotWhat you put in it
subjectThe subject line, which is also the page's title
preheaderThe line an inbox shows after the subject; the message hides it
productThe product's name, the logo's alternative text
logo_urlThe https address where you host the lockup at 128 pixels high: logo/ncode/lockup/ncode-lockup-blue-h128.png, or logo/identity/lockup/ncode-identity-lockup-blue-h128.png for NCode Identity. Under a tenant's colors, take the black lockup, because NCode's marks then go one color (Marks)
logo_widthThe lockup's width at 32 pixels high: 106 for the {N} lockup, 186 for the {id} lockup
headingWhat the message is about, in the heading role
messageOne paragraph, in the body role
action_label, action_urlThe key: what it does, such as "Verify email address", and the https address it opens
codeA value read off the system, such as a one-time code, on a screen
footerWhy the reader got the message, in the ui role, muted
primary, primary_edge, primary_lip, on_primary, screen, on_screenThe key's, its edge's and the screen's colors: the same names, with - for _, in deriveBrand(primary, secondary).light of tokens/derive.mjs, which gives NCode's own colors without a tenant's

Fill the color slots only from deriveBrand(), never from a tenant's color as it was typed. Each slot sits inside a style attribute, where escaping as HTML doesn't stop a value such as red;display:none from adding a declaration: deriveBrand() writes every color as #RRGGBB, and gives NCode Blue for any input that isn't a hexadecimal color. Its guards keep the key's label and the code readable on their colors, and the key's edge reaches 3 to 1 against the card whatever the tenant's color.

Delete the key's table or the code's table when the message has neither: a comment above each marks it.

A Page Without 2024 CSS

Take tokens/tokens.static.css: every token with its color written out, light at the root and dark by the theme, and no light-dark(), relative color or color-mix(). It derives nothing, so a tenant's colors come from tokens/derive.mjs's customProperties().

Slides in Marp

Take slides/instrument.css, the Marp theme instrument, with fonts/OFL-Instrument-Sans.txt and fonts/OFL-Martian-Mono.txt. It embeds both typefaces, so a deck renders in them on any machine and loads no other file, and the SIL Open Font License asks every copy of a font to carry its license. Name the theme in the VS Code extension's markdown.marp.themes setting, or give its path to Marp CLI's --theme-set option, and choose it in the deck's front matter:

---
marp: true
theme: instrument
paginate: true
---

A slide is 1280 by 720 pixels on the light theme's surface, and every type role is 1.75 times its size on a screen: # is the title role, ## heading, ### subheading, running text body, the header, the footer and a table's head label, and the page number a readout. A code block is a screen. <!-- _class: lead --> makes a title slide, its # in the headline role, and <!-- _class: invert --> sets a slide on the dark theme's surface. The theme colors no syntax: Marp Core 4 highlights code with highlight.js and Marp Core 5 with Shiki, so a deck that wants colored code styles it in its own <style>. Put a mark on a slide as an image from logo/, as Marks says (the decision).

A Tool That Reads Design Tokens

Take tokens/tokens.json, in the Design Tokens Community Group format 2025.10. Primitives are at the top level, and the semantic colors and shadows under light and dark. A token a tenant's colors change carries its CSS rule in $extensions["org.ncode.instrument"]. A group that sets a tier names it there, and the groups inside it inherit it.

Take tokens/tokens.resolver.json for a tool that reads the Design Tokens Resolver Module 2025.10. It is one document that references no other file. Its set instrument holds the tokens both themes share. Its modifier theme, light by default or dark, puts that theme's semantic colors and shadows under the group theme, such as theme.color.text (the decision).

Icons

Take icons/sprite.svg beside css/base.css, and use an icon by its symbol, i-<name>:

<svg class="icon" aria-hidden="true"><use href="brand/icons/sprite.svg#i-search"/></svg>

The sprite loads from the page's own origin, under default-src 'self', and .icon gives the icon its size and stroke. Take icons/<name>.svg for one icon alone, and icons/icons.json for a component that draws an icon's shapes inline. Vendor icons/LICENSE-Lucide.txt with any icon from Lucide: Icons says which they are.

A README, a Favicon, a Package Icon

Marks says which file of logo/ncode/ or logo/identity/ each place takes, and how to name a file by its address at a release's tag in a README.

Vendor a Release

Take files from one tagged release, and prove in your own gate that they did not drift.

  1. Copy vendoring/vendor-brand.mjs into your repository. It is Node.js alone, with no packages, and adds nothing to your lockfile. Copy it unchanged: it starts with // Copyright © NCode Group and // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0, so a header check takes it as it is, and it keeps the SHA-256 the release's manifest.json lists for it.

  2. Beside it, write a brand.lock.json that names each file you take, where it goes and where it comes from in the release. Take every file a stylesheet loads, here the four fonts css/fonts.css names, and each font family's license with its fonts:

    {
  "version": "0.10.0",
  "files": {
    "src/brand/tokens/tokens.css": { "source": "tokens/tokens.css", "sha256": "" },
    "src/brand/css/fonts.css": { "source": "css/fonts.css", "sha256": "" },
    "src/brand/fonts/instrument-sans-latin-wdth-normal.woff2": { "source": "fonts/instrument-sans-latin-wdth-normal.woff2", "sha256": "" },
    "src/brand/fonts/instrument-sans-latin-ext-wdth-normal.woff2": { "source": "fonts/instrument-sans-latin-ext-wdth-normal.woff2", "sha256": "" },
    "src/brand/fonts/martian-mono-latin-wdth-normal.woff2": { "source": "fonts/martian-mono-latin-wdth-normal.woff2", "sha256": "" },
    "src/brand/fonts/martian-mono-latin-ext-wdth-normal.woff2": { "source": "fonts/martian-mono-latin-ext-wdth-normal.woff2", "sha256": "" },
    "src/brand/fonts/OFL-Instrument-Sans.txt": { "source": "fonts/OFL-Instrument-Sans.txt", "sha256": "" },
    "src/brand/fonts/OFL-Martian-Mono.txt": { "source": "fonts/OFL-Martian-Mono.txt", "sha256": "" }
  }
}
  3. Run node vendor-brand.mjs --update 0.10.0. It needs the GitHub CLI, gh, signed in with gh auth login, or with GH_TOKEN in CI. It downloads the release's archive, brand-0.10.0.tar.gz, from the GitHub release v0.10.0, and has gh attestation verify prove its build provenance: signed by publish.yml for the tag v0.10.0 on a GitHub-hosted runner. It refuses the archive unless the attestation names its SHA-256, its manifest.json is that version, and it holds every file the manifest lists, at the manifest's size and SHA-256, and nothing else. Only then does it write the files and pin each hash in the lock. A release never changes, so once the lock pins a version, it refuses a file of that version with another hash. It writes nothing outside the lock's folder, by a path or through a symbolic link. --from <file> reads the archive from a file instead, such as one you downloaded, and verifies it the same way.
  4. Run node vendor-brand.mjs --check in your gate and in CI. It needs no network and no GitHub CLI, and fails, naming the file, when a vendored file is missing or differs from the lock.

To move to another release, run --update with its version, and review the diff of the vendored files in the pull request: a value change shows there, line by line. Versions and license says what each kind of version number means.

To check an archive yourself, run gh attestation verify brand-0.10.0.tar.gz --repo NCodeGroup/brand --signer-workflow NCodeGroup/brand/.github/workflows/publish.yml.
